page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized server instance featuring 8 virtual CPUs and 62 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.75 GB per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The processor features a cache hierarchy consisting of a 48 KB L1d cache, a 2 MB L2 cache, and a 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4-highmem-8 demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2270.0 and a text processing score of 3059.0, both placing the instance in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong results, registering at 34.83 GB/sec and 14.96 GB/sec respectively. Multi-core and memory subsystem benchmarks generally align with average mid-tier expectations. The instance achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 7129.54 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8519.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a cached read-only small block speed of 687.78 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write speeds reach 61.4 GB/sec and 35.37 GB/sec.

The instance exhibits specific performance tradeoffs, particularly in large-scale computational tasks. While prompt processing for a 7B LLM model reaches an average speed of 55.58 tokens/sec, text generation for the same model drops to a weak 7.05 tokens/sec, and prompt processing for a 70B model is limited to 5.68 tokens/sec. This indicates a clear bottleneck for larger AI workloads due to the lack of GPU acceleration. However, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications that do not require massive parallel compute. The instance is suited for workloads such as database operations, where it achieves 4132.63 operations on Passmark, Redis key-value stores averaging 12.37 million SET operations per second, text processing, and memory-intensive web serving.
